## Cross-panel ghost interpolation (`interpolate`) {#sec-ch03-csinterp}

Local symbols (flagged to the editor): $\ell = 1..n_g$ the ghost layer counted from the panel edge (count);
$N_{\mathrm{p}}$ the cells along a panel edge, $n_2 p_x$ (count); $\Delta\xi = \pi/(2N_{\mathrm{p}})$ the angular cell
width [rad]; $u$ the fractional source abscissa along the edge, in cells of the source panel [-]; $\eta'$ the
along-edge angle of a ghost centre on the source panel [rad].

### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: a ghost across a panel edge is a linear interpolation along the edge, at an abscissa precomputed once by
mapping the ghost centre onto the neighbouring panel; velocities travel in the global spherical frame.
**Switch**: `SyncOptions.interpolate(true)`, set by the per-stage conserved sync, the initial primitive sync and the
scalar syncs. **Default**: on in those syncs; off for face states and the donor factor. **Requires**:
`interp_order: 2`; a subdivided panel ($p_x > 1$) runs the sync in two phases. **Order**: second (linear
interpolation). **Defining equation**: @eq-ch03-csinterp-weights.
:::

Across a panel edge the two panels' coordinate lines meet at an angle, so a ghost cannot be a copy of a neighbour's
cell. snapy fills each ghost by one-dimensional linear interpolation along the shared edge, from a strip of the
neighbour's cells. The source of a ghost in layer $\ell$ does not sit opposite it: it slides along the edge toward the
edge midpoint by up to $n_g - \tfrac12$ cells, independently of resolution. So the strip is widened by $n_g$ cells on
each side, and when a panel is split among blocks the widened strip reaches into the sender's own intra-panel halo,
which must be current; the sync therefore runs in two phases, intra-panel first. Velocities are rotated from the
sender's panel frame to the global spherical $(r, \theta, \varphi)$ frame before sending and back into the receiver's
frame after interpolation. In the history: [chengcli/snapy#222](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/issues/222) (the
decomposition fixes).

### Derivation

The slide follows from the gnomonic map, as in `sources/canoe__cubedsphere_decomposition_TECH_REPORT.md` §1. Take the
right edge of a panel, $\xi = \pi/4$. A ghost of layer $\ell$ sits at $\xi = \pi/4 + (\ell - \tfrac12)\Delta\xi$ and
along-edge angle $\eta$; its direction is $(1, \tan\xi, \tan\eta)$ in the panel's frame. The neighbouring panel's
frame is the same frame turned by $\pi/2$ about the edge, in which the same direction reads $(\tan\xi, -1, \tan\eta)$
up to sign, so its along-edge angle there is

$$
\tan\eta' = \frac{\tan\eta}{\tan\xi}.
$$ {#eq-ch03-csinterp-slide}

On the edge itself $\tan\xi = 1$ and $\eta' = \eta$. Outside it, with $\varepsilon = (\ell - \tfrac12)\Delta\xi$ and
$\tan\xi = 1 + 2\varepsilon + O(\varepsilon^2)$, expanding gives $\eta' - \eta = -\varepsilon\sin 2\eta +
O(\varepsilon^2)$: a slide of $(\ell - \tfrac12)\sin 2\eta$ cells toward $\eta = 0$, at most $n_g - \tfrac12$ cells,
at the corners. The code does not use the expansion: `cs_build_ghost_usrc` maps each ghost centre through Cartesian
coordinates onto the source panel and converts the angle to a cell abscissa $u = (\eta' + \pi/4)/\Delta\xi - \tfrac12$,
reversed when the edge table says so ([`cubed_sphere_utils.cpp:78-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.cpp#L78-L108)). The ghost value is then

$$
q_{\mathrm{ghost}} = (1 - w)\,q_{\lfloor u\rfloor} + w\,q_{\lfloor u\rfloor + 1}, \qquad w = u - \lfloor u\rfloor,
$$ {#eq-ch03-csinterp-weights}

with the cell index shifted by an integer per block. @eq-ch03-csinterp-weights is the `interp_order == 2` branch of
`_interp_ghost_LR` ([`gnomonic_equiangle.cpp:475-514`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp#L475-L514)) and of `_interp_ghost_BT`
([`gnomonic_equiangle.cpp:516-554`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp#L516-L554)). Linear interpolation is exact for linear data and has an $O(\Delta\xi^2)$
error otherwise. The margin is the largest slide rounded up, $\lceil n_g - \tfrac12\rceil = n_g$, which is
`cs_interp_margin` ([`cubed_sphere_utils.hpp:95-108`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/cubed_sphere_utils.hpp#L95-L108)). For $N_{\mathrm{p}} = 64$ and $n_g = 3$ the exact slide
from @eq-ch03-csinterp-slide is at most 2.4955 cells and departs from the expansion by at most 0.072 cells (check line
`[C11]` of `geometry_check.out`).

The ordering constraint is derived in the same source, §5 and §6: on a subdivided panel the widened strip packed for a
cross-panel neighbour contains cells this block holds only as intra-panel ghosts, and those are written by the unpack
of the same sync. One round cannot satisfy that, so the intra-panel round completes first.

### Numerical method

The abscissae are built once in `reset` for the whole edge (face 0, left side, reused for every edge by symmetry) and
kept as a double per ghost; the block's offset into the edge is kept as a separate integer and added to the index after
`floor`, so the stored weight does not depend on the decomposition. A sync with interpolation on a cubed sphere with
$p_x > 1$ or $p_y > 1$ runs as intra-panel (no interpolation), then cross-panel, then `fill_corners`. In the
cross-panel pack the strip is widened by the margin, its velocities are rotated to the spherical frame (conserved
momenta are raised to contravariant first), and the strip is relabelled for the neighbour's orientation by the
reverse, flip and transpose flags. In the unpack the wide strip lands in the ghost zone and its margin, the ghost is
interpolated from it while all of it is still in the spherical frame, and only the narrow ghost zone is rotated into
the receiver's frame (and lowered back to covariant for conserved momenta). @fig-ch03-csinterp-slide shows the slide.

```{python}
#| label: fig-ch03-csinterp-slide
#| fig-cap: "Two panels meeting at an edge (thick line). Ghost centres of layers $\\ell = 1, 2, 3$ beyond the edge (open circles) and the points of the neighbouring panel they are interpolated from (filled circles), joined by arrows: the sources slide along the edge toward its midpoint, most at the panel corners. Computed from @eq-ch03-csinterp-slide for $N_{\\mathrm{p}} = 16$ cells per edge; both axes are in cells."
#| fig-alt: "Ghost centres in three rows beside a vertical edge, each connected to a source point shifted toward the middle of the edge."
#| echo: false
from snapy_report.ch03.fig_csinterp_slide import make_fig
make_fig()
```

: Code map of the cross-panel interpolation. {#tbl-ch03-csinterp-code}

In step order (@tbl-ch03-csinterp-code):

1. At setup `reset` calls `cs_build_ghost_usrc` for the whole edge and stores the block's slice with the integer
   shift `usrc_shift_LR` ([`gnomonic_equiangle.cpp:162-196`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/coord/gnomonic_equiangle.cpp#L162-L196)).
2. `exchange` splits an interpolating sync on a subdivided panel into `intra_panel_only` and `cross_panel_only`
   rounds and calls `fill_corners` after both ([`meshblock.cpp:554-572`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/mesh/meshblock.cpp#L554-L572)).
3. `serialize` returns after the intra-panel neighbours in phase 1; in phase 2 it widens the strip with `extend_x2`
   or `extend_x3` ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:625-685`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L625-L685)), sets `rev_flag`, `trans_flag` and `flip_flag`
   ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:700-705`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L700-L705)), rotates the velocities with `cs_apply_velocity_transform_`
   ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:736-753`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L736-L753)) and relabels the strip with `flip_out`
   ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:755-780`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L755-L780)).
4. `deserialize` lands the wide strip with `sub_w`, calls `interp_ghost`, then rotates the narrow ghost zone back
   with `cs_apply_velocity_transform_` ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:897-958`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L897-L958)).

: Tests of the cross-panel interpolation. C++ entries carry the build suffix (`.release`). {#tbl-ch03-csinterp-tests}

The bitwise case is `subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block` ([`test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp:159-179`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp#L159-L179));
the deck is the card written by `write_card`, $8\times8$ cells per panel, `nb2` = 1, 2 and 4, all $6p_x^2$ blocks in one
process ([`test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp:20-40`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp#L20-L40)). Its CUDA twin
`subdivided_panel_exchange_matches_one_block_cuda` is in the same binary and skips without a GPU
([`test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp:181-200`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp#L181-L200)). The tag case is `rejects_tags_that_collide_with_the_variable_offset`
([`test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp:150-157`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_cubed_sphere_exchange.cpp#L150-L157)). Their pass status at the pin was not run for this chapter (missing
evidence).

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `interp_order` must be 2; the fourth-order branch of `_interp_ghost_LR` and `_interp_ghost_BT` is unreachable.
- Bitwise decomposition independence is tested for `nb2` = 1, 2, 4 in one process, one stage.
:::

The source report records bit-for-bit agreement of `nb2` = 1, 2 and 4 over one cycle on CPU with gloo and one block
per rank (`sources/canoe__cubedsphere_decomposition_TECH_REPORT.md` §7 and §10); that was measured on a development
build, not at the pin, and re-running it at the pin needs the report's multi-rank gate, which is not committed. The
margin cells of the wide landing zone keep the neighbour's spherical frame after the unpack; the same report shows
with a gate that nothing reads them (§8), which was not re-checked at the pin. `_interpolate_to_local` is a stub with a
TODO and no effect ([`cubed_sphere_layout.cpp:1065-1088`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/src/layout/cubed_sphere_layout.cpp#L1065-L1088)). `DeviceTest.interpolate_LR` sets up linear data
and asserts nothing, as written in `interpolate_LR` ([`test_coordinate.cpp:424-506`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_coordinate.cpp#L424-L506)). The switch combinations
that are tested are listed in the switch coverage matrix, @sec-ch12-matrix.
